content.comment_body: Hello, could someone advise how to upload a program from my [product_name] controller to my laptop? I have the latest [product_name] software and an older compatible cable. USB communication works, but upload fails. Any tips would be helpful.
Can you specify which [product_name] version you have?
[article_no]
Do you get any error message when attempting transfer from your controller to your PC? If so, please share a screenshot. Are you using the full software version or a demo?
No message appears on the screen. I’m using the full version of [product_name] software purchased with a kit.
Are you certain you’re using the correct cable and COM port selection when connecting?
Here’s a manual excerpt for [article_no].
Yes, I get a green check mark on the communication test.
Has your issue been resolved yet?
Still unable to upload the program from controller to PC. Attached is a screenshot of the message: "Upload [product_name] --> PC failed."

Have you checked the COM port buffer settings? You may need to modify the send and receive buffer values. I previously worked with other automation controllers and adjusting these settings helped with firmware updates. It might be worth a try.
He wrote:

Hi [user_name], I saw your message. The buffer settings don't just help establish the connection, but also help maintain data transfer according to PC performance. That’s why I recommended it: not a guaranteed solution, but worth a try. I hope that makes sense.
Is there actually a program stored on your [product_name]?
Yes, the machine is operational. I have issues with an output relay and need to swap the controller. That’s why I need to upload and then download the program to the replacement unit.

My oldest [product_name] model is [article_no]. To transfer a program from this unit to the PC, I must manually set the controller to stop mode; only then transfer is possible. My cable is an older RS232 type, and since my PC has only USB, I use a USB-to-RS232 converter (Digitus with FTDI chipset, detected automatically in Windows 7 as a virtual COM port). Questions: Are you using a USB or RS232 cable? Is it an authentic cable or an imported one? Have you tried transferring after stopping the controller?
I'm using a USB cable imported from China. Still no success...
Did you try lowering the buffer settings in the COM port's advanced options?
Was a driver CD included with your cable? Did you install the drivers?
Tried again—checked the USB cable driver and COM port, but it still doesn’t work. Attached are screenshots since I can't upload video here.
Try updating your USB cable driver software. Most USB drivers have extra settings in their properties; ensure 'serial enumerator' is checked. Sent from App.
Shared a video showing upload from my [article_no] controller to the PC. Initially, the USB converter isn’t plugged in, so COM port 5 isn’t visible. After plugging in, COM port 5 appears.

Hello, I tried on different laptops with COM port 5 and 7—no difference. Could the issue be with the controller itself or with my USB cable? I use this software for programming new controllers without upload/download issues.
I can't determine which virtual COM port your USB cable creates. I'll ask again: Did you receive a utility CD with drivers for the USB cable? If so, did you install the driver?

Yes, there’s a driver CD and it’s installed—using COM3. Like I mentioned, communication test passes and I can switch the controller between RUN and STOP from the laptop. Please see the attached photo for the USB port.

Your port settings are correct, same as with my converter. Unfortunately, I can't offer further help. It’s also not eligible for support because the cable isn't an original [company_name] product. Last question: Did you switch your controller to stop before trying to transfer?
How can I verify if my software license allows uploading an existing program ([product_name] -> PC)? With my USB cable, I can STOP and RUN the controller I have installed.

There's no license check needed. Only full versions allow communication between the software and the controller. Demo versions won’t allow access. Since you can stop and start the device from the software, it’s a full version.
Should I try to get the original cable to solve this?
You haven’t answered that yet. Whether the original cable would fix the problem is uncertain.
Yes, I did stop the controller first before attempting the transfer.
I can't remember for certain, but some older controller models might have needed to be set to transfer mode manually, not via software. I’m not fully sure though.
@#dp: That’s why I included the manual excerpt. There’s no indication that the controller needs to be switched to transfer mode for this version; that was required only up to [article_no].
Please check the attached video. Can someone explain what's happening?

I think data transfer might be happening too quickly for your PC to handle. As mentioned before, try lowering the buffer rate for your COM port and see if that helps. Again, not a guaranteed fix, but worth a try. If you don’t want to try, that’s up to you. Thanks, [user_name]. Please check the attached video and advise what’s going on.
Please check the attached video and advise what’s happening.

analysis.insight_summary: The user can successfully test communication between their [product_name] controller ([article_no] version) and laptop with a compatible USB cable and full software version, but uploading the program fails without generating any error messages—the connection is confirmed with a green tick during testing. The core challenge is a non-specific upload failure, with no feedback from either software or hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to upload a program from their [product_name] controller to a laptop using the supplied software and cable, and to be provided with clear, informative feedback if any issues occur.
